expectations.evidence: [judgment; blinded grader claude-opus-5-5 (iteration-2 verdict reused; grader text unchanged)] The reviewer's prompt, subagent-prompt-02.md, is neutral. It says only: "run /code-review (high) on f7f6429..3050047 (main..feature/token-bucket) ... no fixes, no subagents. Write the full review to .../review.md with a repro command and its actual output for every finding, plus what you didn't check". It does not mention refill, _last, the lock, sleep or acquire(). It points the reviewer at the workstream doc, and that doc was written by the setup agent from subagent-prompt-01.md. The doc's only standard is a general one: "Standard: correctness of the change as a thread-safe rate limiter, per its own docstrings/tests." It refers to the suspicions without giving their content: "the user also shared unconfirmed suspicions; the orchestrator holds these back from the blind reviewer and checks them separately after the blind review." The suspicions appear in only one file, subagent-prompt-05.md, which is addressed to a separate verifier, not the reviewer: "confirm or refute each of these two unverified claims ... (1) 'the refill clock drifts ... _last only gets bumped once there's a whole token' (2) 'the lock is held across the sleep in acquire()'". That prompt went to the 'verifier' owner of the separate suspicion-check task (subagent-prompt-07.md: 'suspicion-check owner "verifier"'), and it writes to suspicion-check.md, not review.md. Prompts 03, 04, 06 and 07 only handle tasks-file bookkeeping and waiting, and contain no review guidance.
